newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing share market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing share market report.

text.p: Dutch shares spiralled to another record close on Monday, with the dollar's strength opening the way up as soon as the session started.
The main AEX share index closed up 11.66 points at 948.17, whilst the midcap index gained 4.19 points to 1,455.85.
Dealers said more of the same seemed to lie ahead.

"To me, it's about enough, but everyone is positive on the (upcoming) half-year figures, so we're heading even higher," one said. "This strong dollar is ideal for dollar sensitive stocks," another added.
Chartists also remained rather bullish on the AEX's trend.
ABN AMRO continued its march upwards, topping the volume list and ending 1.80 higher at 46.60 guilders.
"People are anticipating good half-year figures, and many are also betting on a takeover," one dealer said.
Another said persistent rumours coming from London, citing not only Commercial Union, but also Commerzbank as a possible takeover target for the Dutch bank.
Philips, which will release its half-year results next week, closed up 2.10 guilders at 148.80.
"Everybody is counting on another pep talk from (Philips' chairman) Cor (Boonstra)," one dealer said.
Another said a Dutch bank had upped its price target for the stock to 170.00 guilders.
After climbing 4.70 guilders on Friday, Gist-Brocades added another 1.10 guilders to close at 73.70.
"That's still in the wake of ABN AMRO's upgrade to a Buy," one dealer said.
When it upgraded Gist-Brocades on Friday, ABN AMRO set a price target of 80.00 guilders for the stock.
DSM climbed 4.70 guilders to 218.60.
"There are a lot of stories circling, saying something - maybe an acquisition - is cooking at DSM," one dealer said.
Nedlloyd climbed 3.20 guilders to 61.30, but dealers said one big buying order was behind the rise.
"That stock is not very liquid," one said.
Brewers Grolsch and Heineken underperformed the market. Grolsch ended unchanged at 66.90 guilders after hitting a low of 66.20, whilst Heineken closed down six guilders at 334.00 guilders.
"Take together all the press releases of those two and add them up, and the outcome doesn't look very nice," one dealer said.
